prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Generate ONE finished wide editorial blog cover as a matching next volume in the same visual series as the supplied reference cover. The reference image is the exact STYLE, PALETTE, MATERIAL, FRAME and ASPECT RATIO reference; preserve these carefully. New topic is Agent Loop: thinking, taking action with tools, receiving results, then thinking again.

Format: panoramic 5:2 / 2.5:1 landscape, ideally 2000x800. No typography, no words, no letters, no numbers, no watermark. This is a full-bleed fine-art cover, NOT a white-background character illustration.

Series design to match: muted olive-green weathered stone/marble outer field; generous inset pale warm ivory parchment panel with rounded rectangular corners, delicate double antique-gold hairline border, tiny four-point gold ornaments at top and bottom center. Antique Renaissance copperplate engraving / classical fresco / banknote etching, realistic sculptural hands with finely crosshatched anatomy, rich yet desaturated textile drapes, olive branches in opposite corners, faded grey-green botanical/cloud engraving at the panel margins. Warm ivory, sage olive, muted slate blue and restrained old gold. Match the sophisticated texture and spacious balanced composition of the reference rather than modern digital concept art.

New central image: two large beautifully engraved Renaissance hands enter from the left and right edges, left sleeve muted slate blue, right sleeve warm ivory, hands subtly rotated to gently guide an elegant thin golden ORBIT between them. The orbit is a large airy horizontal elliptical loop, rendered as two or three exceptionally fine old-gold strands, with THREE small antique round medallions embedded on the loop at separated positions: an engraved radiant mind/star symbol (thinking), a tiny crossed wrench-and-quill emblem (tool action), and an unfurled scroll emblem (result/feedback). These are simple etched pictograms, not company logos. The circulating gold strands have a few subtle particle dots and tiny leaf-shaped arrowheads that make returning feedback perceptible, but must feel like celestial mechanics in an old scientific manuscript, never a formal flowchart. The two hands actively guide the orbit with poised fingers. Fine faint radiating construction lines emerge from fingers as in the reference. The center remains airy and quiet, with generous parchment negative space. No complex clockwork, no gears pile, no big central machinery, no cartoon character. Place three smaller decorative medallion-like rosettes along the lower center to echo the previous cover's visual rhythm, but keep them visually subordinate to the orbit. Preserve safe margins and all corner framing.

Keep the reference's visual lineage unmistakable: classical engraved hands, antique book cover, olive stone border, ivory parchment, hairline gilding, restrained botanical corners. Invent the loop motif for this chapter; do not reproduce the original straight left-to-right streaming waveform.
